pins.name: D0
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Commonly wired to a FLASH/BOOT button on dev boards. On this board it is the schematic-confirmed KEY_FLASH pushbutton (see NOTE above)
KEY_FLASH — onboard user pushbutton (schematic-confirmed, see NOTE above)

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D2
pins.label: D2 (GPIO2)
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. Commonly wired to the on-board LED on dev boards

pins.name: D3
pins.label: D3 (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D15
pins.label: D15 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D16
pins.label: GPIO16 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake. On this board it drives the schematic-confirmed active-low BLUE status LED (see NOTE above)
Onboard BLUE status LED, active-low (schematic-confirmed, see NOTE above). LED_BUILTIN in this board's pins_arduino.h

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Native range is 0-1.0V on the bare chip; this board adds an on-board 400K/100K divider extending the externally-exposed A0/ADC_EX pin's range to 0-5.0V (see adc NOTE below) — check your board's documentation before wiring higher voltages
